---
title: "Getting started"
---

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install "slenderpy @ git+https://github.com/rte-france/pallas-slenderpy"
```

The examples and the documentation also use matplotlib
(`pip install "slenderpy[examples] @ git+..."`).

## The building blocks

Every solver takes the same two descriptions of the structure, both frozen
dataclasses of [](`slenderpy.components`):

- a [](`~slenderpy.components.Conductor`): mass per unit length, diameter,
  axial and bending stiffnesses;
- a [](`~slenderpy.components.Span`): length, tension, support level
  difference and, for a beam, its boundary conditions.

Time-domain solvers take a [](`~slenderpy.simulation.Parameters`) (number of
nodes, time window, time and output steps, stored positions) and return a
[](`~slenderpy.simulation.Results`) indexed by time and span fraction. Loads
are forces from [](`slenderpy.force.core`), or any function with the same
signature.

## A first cable run

A 400 m span released from a perturbed catenary, mid-span position over 20 s:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from slenderpy import simulation
from slenderpy.cable import dynamic
from slenderpy.components import Conductor, Span

conductor = Conductor(mass=1.571, diameter=0.0313, axial_stiffness=3.76e07)
span = Span(length=400.0, tension=3.7e04)
parameters = simulation.Parameters(ns=101, tf=20.0, dt=2.0e-03, dr=2.0e-02, los=[0.5])

x, y, z = dynamic.equilibrium(conductor, span, parameters.ns)
bump = 0.5 * np.sin(np.pi * x / span.length)
res = dynamic.solve(
    conductor, span, parameters, initial_position=np.stack([x, y + bump, z + bump])
)

plt.plot(res.lot(), res["y"].values[:, 0], label="y (out of plane)")
plt.plot(res.lot(), res["z"].values[:, 0] - z[parameters.ns // 2], label="z - static")
plt.xlabel("time (s)")
plt.ylabel("mid-span (m)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

## A first beam run

A 20 m clamped span under its weight: static shape, then released from 1.5
times that shape with the Bouc-Wen law, whose hysteresis damps the vibration:

```{python}
from slenderpy.beam.dynamic import solve_dynamic
from slenderpy.beam.static import shape
from slenderpy.boundary_condition import clamped
from slenderpy.force.core import Gravity

conductor = Conductor(mass=1.57, ei_min=28.28, ei_max=2155.07, beta_flexion=6.438e-07)
span = Span(length=20.0, tension=2.0e03, boundary_conditions=clamped())
parameters = simulation.Parameters(ns=501, tf=10.0, dt=2.0e-03, dr=1.0e-02, los=[0.5])

rest = shape.solve(conductor, span, np.full(501, -9.81 * conductor.mass), 501, model="varying")
res = solve_dynamic(
    conductor, span, parameters, model="varying",
    force=Gravity(conductor.mass), initial_position=1.5 * rest,
)

plt.plot(res.lot(), 1e3 * (res["z"].values[:, 0] - rest[250]))
plt.xlabel("time (s)")
plt.ylabel("mid-span z - static (mm)")
plt.show()
```
